jobs.description_text: Scope of the Role: We are recruiting US-based architects and certified plans examiners to evaluate the output of an AI system that performs automated building-code compliance review on architectural permit applications. The system ingests permit submissions — new builds, alterations, modifications — and issues a compliant or non-compliant determination for each applicable check, drawn from the International Building Code. Every determination comes with a cited code provision and a marked location on the drawing set showing the evidence relied upon. Your job is to tell us where the system got it wrong. You are applying the same judgment you already apply in plan review or permit preparation, to a set of determinations that have already been made. Where the system is correct, you confirm it. Where it is wrong, you correct it and the correction becomes training signal. This is expert review work, not data entry. There is no volume of repetitive clicking to grind through and no generalist labeling pool to compete with — the entire premise of the program is that these judgments cannot be made by anyone without real code expertise. What You’ll Own: Review and correct pass/fail verdicts, written rationales, and citation boxes on PDF plans using the in-tool editing toolkit. Innodata builds that data and those evaluations for the customers and frontier labs advancing speech and audio models, and we are hiring a Research Scientist to own the science behind it. You will partner directly with the customers and frontier labs building ASR, text-to-speech, speech-to-speech and conversational voice, diarization, and audio-language models, as interested in the data behind them as in the models themselves. Your work is judgment: which conditions and languages a benchmark must cover to be honest, what a transcription convention should be for a given objective, and when an automated metric can be trusted versus when a human ear is required. You will also partner closely with our transcription and linguistics lead, whose standards directly shape what the models learn. jobs.title: Research Scientist, Video & Multimodal
jobs.description_text: Scope of the Role: Video is where multimodal models are weakest and hardest to grade. Temporal reasoning, long-form understanding, grounding events in time, and holding audio, video, and text together do not fall out of image benchmarks — and the evaluations for them are still immature. Closing that gap is gated as much by how we design data and evaluation as by architecture. Innodata builds that data and those evaluations for the customers and frontier labs advancing video and multimodal models, and we are hiring a Research Scientist to own the science behind it. You will partner directly with the customers and frontier labs building video understanding, video-language, and video-generation models, as interested in the data behind them as in the models themselves. Video spans two model families judged in completely different ways: models that understand video — answering questions, localizing events, grounding language in time — where the question is whether the answer is correct; and models that generate it, where fidelity, temporal coherence, and physical plausibility matter and no automatic metric is settled. You own the evaluation science for both, and knowing when model-based scoring can stand in for a human versus when it can't. Your conclusions shape what our partners measure and collect next. jobs.description_text: About the Role Complaints and disputes are where Kikoff finds out what it is actually doing for its customers. They also arrive with a clock attached: the law, the regulators, and our bank partner each set deadlines, and none of them move. Reporting to the Head of Compliance, you will own the way we manage and respond to complaints and disputes. This role brings dedicated ownership for a program that scales with our products and our customers. You will mature Kikoff's complaints and disputes framework, strengthen how it operates in the hands of the Customer Experience team who interact with our customers, and make it hold as volume grows. You start as an individual contributor and hire an analyst as volume requires. The work is equal parts operating discipline and investigation: hitting every deadline is table stakes, and the value is in what the pattern of complaints and disputes tells us to go fix. jobs.title: Senior Photonics Circuit Design Engineer
jobs.description_text: The Laser System Architecture & Engineering (LSAE) team is seeking a Photonics Circuit Design Engineer. The candidate will design and model the photonic and analog sub-circuits that make up Lightmatter's Guide™ laser products and Passage™ optical links. Examples include the laser source and wavelength-locking blocks, ring filter and modulator banks, mux/demux, optical power splitting and monitoring, and the photodetector-receiver front end. You will own the bridge between device physics and sub-circuit behavior. You will build high-fidelity behavioral models that capture fabrication variability, dispersion and thermal effects. From them you will assemble sub-circuit models that accurately predict how each block performs. Systems architects will build their end-to-end product simulations on your models, so your models must be accurate, correlated to silicon, and ready to plug into larger simulations. Responsibilities Construct and maintain high-fidelity compact and behavioral representations for both active and passive silicon photonic elements, covering waveguides, couplers, MZIs, micro-rings, multiplexers, phase control elements, thermal tuners, modulators, detectors, and integrated III-V/SOA components. Incorporate process variations (waveguide geometry and etch biases), dispersion metrics, thermal-optical tuning characteristics, and non-linear properties directly into component modeling. We are seeking a Senior ML Scientist to connect that work to human medicine, building the systems that assess whether a clinical program's biology holds up. Three questions define the work. Is the mechanism well supported? What has actually been established about how this intervention is meant to work, and what has only been assumed. Does the mechanism operate in patients? Human genetics, expression, cohort and prior-trial evidence all bear on whether the biology that works in a model system is present, and rate-limiting, in the population being treated. Is the trial built for that mechanism? Endpoints that read out the right thing on the right timescale, biomarkers that measure what the mechanism actually does, and enrollment criteria that select patients in whom it is operative — or, very often, none of these. You will not answer these program by program yourself. You will build the systems that do it, drawing on the mechanistic models and structured biological evidence the rest of the group generates, and grounding them in human data.
